title: Two arms over the belt
subtitle: 2 x UR5e + 2F-85, humanoid mount, head camera
summary: A humanoid-style sorting cell: two UR5e + 2F-85 mounted on the sides of a torso at shoulder height (each arm's base axis pointing outward), the conveyor from the conveyor example in front, and a D435-class colour camera in the head looking down at the belt. The arms come calibrated from the bench (the UR5e + 2F-85 example); this is the deployment calibration: where each arm is really mounted, and the head camera's intrinsics and pose, from tags on the grippers and on the belt.

model.source: Menagerie ur5e + 2f85 (bam_arm.cell's attach) x 2, sysid's conveyor.xml, one MuJoCo camera

cameras.name: head_camera
cameras.source: a D435 colour stream at 640 x 480 (intel_rgbd's sensor contract), as a MuJoCo fovy camera

known.note: the arms' joint zeros and TCPs (bench-calibrated, the UR5e + 2F-85 example), the conveyor's radius (the conveyor example) and the tags' printed geometry
known.pose_correction: a pose correction is a world-frame translation (dx, dy, dz) and rotation vector (rx, ry, rz) applied to the drawn pose: R = exp([r]) R_drawn

gripper_tag.note: a 40 mm tag on the gripper body, 70 mm out along the tool axis, facing the tool's +x

belt_tags.note: tags printed on the belt (belt frame: x along travel, y across)

tree.title: torso (the two shoulder mounts and the head)
belt conveyor (calibrated in the conveyor example)

coverage.function: sysid adapter: the corners' image cells (8 x 6) x depth bands (< 0.8, 0.8-1.1, > 1.1 m)
coverage.rule: share of the 144 (image cell, depth band) cells the planned tag corners fall in; the camera card's scene conditions other than distance are not planned

rungs.name: Nominal kinematics (URDF / DH)
rungs.equation: tool = base · FK(q; nominal DH) · tool frame

references.title: Denavit, Hartenberg (1955). A kinematic notation for lower-pair mechanisms based on matrices. Journal of Applied Mechanics.
Universal Robots (2026). DH parameters for calculations of kinematics and dynamics.
Hollerbach, Wampler (1996). The calibration index and taxonomy for robot kinematic calibration methods. The International Journal of Robotics Research.
Hayati (1983). Robot arm geometric link parameter estimation. The 22nd IEEE Conference on Decision and Control.
Okamura, Park (1996). Kinematic calibration using the product of exponentials formula. Robotica.
Hollerbach, Khalil, Gautier (2016). Model identification. In Springer Handbook of Robotics, 2nd ed. Springer.

rungs.name: + joint compliance and link inertials (today's model)
rungs.equation: tool = FK(q + δq; DH + δDH) · tool frame; joints are servo twins

references.title: Spong (1987). Modeling and control of elastic joint robots. Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement, and Control.
Atkeson, An, Hollerbach (1986). Estimation of inertial parameters of manipulator loads and links. The International Journal of Robotics Research.
Gautier, Khalil (1990). Direct calculation of minimum set of inertial parameters of serial robots. IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation.
Swevers, Ganseman, Tükel, De Schutter, Van Brussel (1997). Optimal robot excitation and identification. IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation.

rungs.name: + joint compliance that grows with use (Archard)

references.title: Archard (1953). Contact and rubbing of flat surfaces. Journal of Applied Physics.
Flodin, Andersson (1997). Simulation of mild wear in spur gears. Wear.

rungs.name: Grey-box residual on M3.wear
rungs.equation: M3.wear + MLP residual (residual joint torques (N·m)) from 3 samples of joint 1 error, joint 2 error, joint 3 error, joint 4 error, joint 5 error, joint 6 error, joint 1 speed, joint 2 speed, joint 3 speed, joint 4 speed, joint 5 speed, joint 6 speed, joint 1 torque, joint 2 torque, joint 3 torque, joint 4 torque, joint 5 torque, joint 6 torque

references.title: Nguyen-Tuong, Peters (2010). Using model knowledge for learning inverse dynamics. IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation.
Zeng, Song, Lee, Rodriguez, Funkhouser (2020). TossingBot: learning to throw arbitrary objects with residual physics. IEEE Transactions on Robotics.

rungs.name: Arm network (black box)
rungs.equation: MLP over 3 samples of joint 1 error, joint 2 error, joint 3 error, joint 4 error, joint 5 error, joint 6 error, joint 1 speed, joint 2 speed, joint 3 speed, joint 4 speed, joint 5 speed, joint 6 speed → joint torques (N·m)

references.title: Hwangbo, Lee, Dosovitskiy, Bellicoso, Tsounis, Koltun, Hutter (2019). Learning agile and dynamic motor skills for legged robots. Science Robotics.
Zhang (2000). A flexible new technique for camera calibration. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence.

rungs.name: + Brown-Conrady distortion
rungs.equation: radial (k1, k2, k3) and tangential (p1, p2) distortion

references.title: Brown (1966). Decentering distortion of lenses. Photogrammetric Engineering.
Heikkilä, Silvén (1997). A four-step camera calibration procedure with implicit image correction. IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.
Zhang (2000). A flexible new technique for camera calibration. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence.

rungs.name: + exposure response and latency (today's model)
rungs.equation: p = K [R | t] X, distorted by (k1, k2, p1, p2, k3)

references.title: Zhang (2000). A flexible new technique for camera calibration. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence.

rungs.name: Rolling shutter: + line delay
rungs.equation: row v exposed at t0 + v · line_delay

references.title: Oth, Furgale, Kneip, Siegwart (2013). Rolling shutter camera calibration. IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.
Meingast, Geyer, Sastry (2005). Geometric models of rolling-shutter cameras. arXiv:cs/0503076.

rungs.name: + a mount that loosens over vibration hours

references.title: Junker (1969). New criteria for self-loosening of fasteners under vibration. SAE Technical Paper.
Whitmore (1995). Estimating degradation by a Wiener diffusion process subject to measurement error. Lifetime Data Analysis.

rungs.name: Grey-box residual on M3.wear
rungs.equation: M3.wear + MLP residual (residual ray offset (px)) from 1 samples of pixel u, pixel v

references.title: Schöps, Larsson, Pollefeys, Sattler (2020). Why having 10,000 parameters in your camera model is better than twelve. IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.

notes: The arms' joint zeros and TCPs are the bench calibration's (the UR5e + 2F-85 example); the belt's travel is the conveyor example's.
The pixels are tag-corner detections simulated as projections plus 0.3 px noise, not rendered images (no detector in the loop).
